steps: CART STORE (new file, e.g. src/lib/cart.ts): a small browser cart keyed by catalogue reference. Store ONLY { ref (use ShopProduct.slug or id), quantity } entries plus enough display metadata (name, formattedPrice) to render the cart list. NEVER derive or store any amount the browser computes for payment - display uses Wix's passthrough formattedPrice strings only, and these NEVER go to the server. Persist in localStorage (or sessionStorage) under a namespaced key like 'wecare.cart.v1'. Export pure functions: addItem(product, qty), setQuantity(ref, qty), removeItem(ref), readCart(), clearCart(), and a toLineItems() that maps the cart to the checkout `create` payload shape [{ catalogReference/productId/slug, quantity }] carrying refs+quantities ONLY. Read amplify/functions/ecommerce/checkout/handler.py and lambda_utils/ecommerce/wix_ecom.create_checkout to confirm the exact lineItems field names the server expects, and match them; if the exact Wix reference field is ambiguous from the code, send the product's Wix catalogue id under the field wix_ecom expects and note the assumption in findings. ADD-TO-CART AFFORDANCE on the product detail page src/pages/shop/[slug].tsx: replace or supplement the current `Ask about <name>` link so the page leads to the cart. Honor the design system exactly (see the extensive inline comments in that file): LIME (#d1f470) is the single actionable surface per page, so the primary add-to-cart button takes the existing .shopd-cta lime treatment (min-height 52px, 2px lime border, #1a3a2a text, :global() wrapping for the styled-jsx scope, opaque #1a3a2a focus ring). Keep the Product structured data (ShopProductHead) and the honest boundary note intact - but UPDATE the copy in .shopd-note and the header docblock so it no longer claims 'This page is not a checkout' once a cart path exists; the note must remain truthful about payment not being live yet (see disabled-initiation handling below). Do not break the two-band structure sectioncheck.js measures or the 108px/96px header clearance.

ADD-TO-CART on the grid src/pages/shop/index.tsx is OPTIONAL for this slice: if adding a per-card action, keep it visually subordinate to the single lime CTA rule (the card's existing accent is the 3px spine; do not put lime on every card). SIGN-IN / REGISTER STEP built on src/lib/customerAuth.ts (new page under a customer-session route, e.g. src/pages/account/sign-in.tsx OR a step embedded in the cart page - choose one and keep it minimal): collect a mobile number, call requestOtp(normaliseMobile(input)); render the masked destination and an OTP input; call submitOtp(mobile, code, session) - null means wrong code with attempts left (invite retry, reuse nextSessionFrom if an error carried a session), a returned CustomerSession means signed in (storeSession is already called inside submitOtp). Handle the requestOtp `registered:false` case HONESTLY: per customerAuth.ts, an unknown number still returns a masked challenge and no code is ever sent, so the UI must NOT claim a code was sent to an unregistered number - instead route unregistered numbers through the registration front door (POST {NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE}/auth/customer-registration with {action:'request', phone} then {action:'verify', phone, code}) to create the customer, then complete sign-in via customerAuth. Read amplify/functions/auth/customer-registration/handler.py for the request/verify contract and response shapes. Do NOT reimplement OTP crypto; only call the documented endpoints/functions.

AUTH GATE: the checkout `create` endpoint requires an authenticated customer (customer_auth.require_customer) and a public visitor cannot check out. So the cart's 'proceed to checkout' must, when getSession() returns null, send the shopper to the sign-in/register step first and return them to the cart afterward (preserve the cart across the redirect via storage; carry a return path). When getSession() is non-null, proceed directly.

CART REVIEW PAGE (new customer-session route, e.g. src/pages/cart.tsx or src/pages/checkout/cart.tsx): render the cart items (name + Wix formattedPrice for display only), quantity controls (setQuantity/removeItem), an empty-cart state, and a single primary 'Proceed to checkout' action honoring the one-lime-CTA rule. On proceed: ensure a session (auth gate above), then POST toLineItems() as { action:'create', lineItems } to {NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE}/ecommerce/checkout with Authorization: Bearer <getSession().accessToken>, mirroring the fetch shape in checkout/status.tsx. The browser sends refs+quantities ONLY - assert this in a test.

HANDLE THE CREATE RESPONSE TRUTHFULLY (this is the core honesty requirement): map the documented responses from checkout/handler.py: (a) status 'PAYMENT_INITIATION_DISABLED' (HTTP 200) -> show a clear, non-alarming state that says checkout is prepared but live payment is not being accepted yet, and does NOT imply a charge happened or offer a fake pay button. Prefer routing to the existing hosted status screen /checkout/status/?a=<paymentAttemptId> (its viewFor() already maps PAYMENT_INITIATION_DISABLED to the neutral 'unavailable' view) OR render an equivalent honest inline state - choose the path that reuses the hosted screen where possible and document the choice. (b) status 'payment_unavailable' / readiness blocked (HTTP 409) -> 'Payments are temporarily unavailable. No charge was made.' (c) 'PAYMENT_REQUEST_SENT' (HTTP 200) -> route to /checkout/status/?a=<paymentAttemptId>. (d) 'SEND_FAILED' (HTTP 502) -> offer retry, no charge. (e) LINE_ITEMS_REQUIRED/empty cart -> empty state. (f) UNSUPPORTED_CURRENCY/AMOUNT_NOT_SETTLED/CATALOGUE_UNAVAILABLE -> honest error copy. (g) 401 (no/invalid session) -> send to sign-in. NEVER present a button that claims to take payment while initiation is off.

Do NOT import components/Layout, Header, Footer, or SupportWidget into the new pages (they are mounted centrally in _app.tsx; PublicRouteRegistration.test.ts forbids per-page chrome imports). === SEMANTIC REVIEW ROUND (2026-09-30-224405-review.md, verdict NEEDS_CHANGES) ===

ISSUE 1 (likely-blocking) FIXED - register-then-sign-in replayed the wrong code. In src/pages/account/sign-in.tsx, the unregistered path used to POST {action:'verify'}, then in finishSignIn() call requestOtp() (which triggers a NEW Cognito CUSTOM_AUTH challenge that sends a SECOND, DIFFERENT WhatsApp code) and immediately submitOtp() with the SAME registration code the shopper had already consumed at verify. Two different codes => submitOtp returned null and the freshly-provisioned customer could never complete sign-in, with no UI state prompting for the second code. FIX: the post-registration Cognito sign-in is now its own OTP step. After {action:'verify'} succeeds, submitCode() calls requestOtp(normalised) to START the Cognito challenge, stores its session+masked destination, CLEARS the code input, and transitions to a new 'signin-code' phase that tells the shopper 'You're all set up. We've sent a new code over WhatsApp ... to sign you in.' The shopper enters THAT code, which is answered via the shared submitOtp(normalised, code, session) branch against the Cognito session - the registration code is never replayed. finishSignIn() was removed; the register path now shares the same submitOtp branch as the registered path. No OTP crypto was reimplemented; only the documented requestOtp/submitOtp and the /auth/customer-registration request/verify endpoints are called.

ISSUE 2 (lower severity) ADDRESSED with a documented guard-comment. The registered:false branch in startPhone() discards challenge.session and routes to registration. Added a SAFETY CONTRACT comment stating this is correct ONLY while the CreateAuthChallenge trigger guarantees it sends NO WhatsApp code when it reports registered:false (i.e. registered:false means 'no live code outstanding', never 'a code was sent to a real customer'); if the trigger ever changes to send a code alongside registered:false, the branch must switch to honouring challenge.session to avoid stranding a real customer. This matches the trigger contract today, so a comment rather than a runtime guard is the right, minimal response (there is no client-side signal that could distinguish the two cases anyway).

ISSUE 3 (documented assumption, NO code change - justified) catalogReference is a flat product id, not the nested Wix {catalogItemId, appId} shape. The review explicitly ACCEPTS this as a documented assumption to revisit when real products replace the dummies, and the user's steering confirms the seven products are placeholders. The assumption is already clearly documented in src/lib/cart.ts (the lineItems-shape docblock) and in these findings. It is safe because (a) the server computes the authoritative total in paise from a live Wix checkout regardless of the reference form, and (b) the payload remains refs+quantities only (no financial figure), which the CartCheckout price-boundary tests assert. Changing it now would require inventing the real nested Wix reference for dummy products, which is not knowable from this repo. So it is left as-is per the review, and remaps trivially once real products are chosen. [STEERING: user confirmed products are dummy - the wiring is fully product-agnostic and no product-specific behaviour was added.]

TESTS ADDED - src/test/AccountSignIn.test.tsx (4 tests, mirrors CartCheckout.test.tsx mocked-customerAuth/mocked-fetch style, drives the whole /account/sign-in page which was previously untested): (1) registered happy path - requestOtp registered:true -> submitOtp against that session -> redirect to return path, front door never touched; (2) registered wrong-code retry - submitOtp returns null -> 'was not right' copy, no navigation; (3) THE register-then-sign-in path - requestOtp registered:false -> front-door request -> verify -> requestOtp (second Cognito challenge) -> the SECOND code is collected and submitOtp is asserted to be called with the Cognito code + Cognito session, NOT the registration code; (4) front-door verify rejected -> honest error, submitOtp never called.
